sentences.text: Oxyosteus was a trout-sized, highly compressed arthrodire placoderm found in Late Devonian Europe.
Living animals would have looked superficially like modern needlefish or houndfish.
The animal is distinguished by very thin plates and a dermal surface covered in small, closely packed tubercles.
Species possessed an extremely compressed body, a pointed elongated snout, and very large eyes.
The skull length of Oxyosteus rostratus ranges from 11 to 13 cm.
The holotype skull of Oxyosteus magnus is 18 cm long.
The genus was first described by Jaekel in 1911.
The parent group of Oxyosteus is Titanichthyidae.
Oxyosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
The genus was originally in its own family but was later merged into the family Brachydeiridae.
Fossils date from the Middle to Late Frasnian periods.
An unnamed species was found in Middle Frasnian strata in the Holy Cross Mountains of Poland.
The group lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago during the Frasnian.
